data: Overall, 10/10 Highly recommend: Great game, atmosphere and story
It is a great game with a great story and gameplay
Amazing immersive experience, great story and great graphics
It is very fun, and challenging
10/10 would highly recommend this game and especially the DLC
Unfortunately this makes the game unplayable for me
Unfortunately, the combat is just awful
Most quests are simply boring and feel like a waste of time
This was the worst waste of time and money ever
Gameplay is very limited, buggy and repetitive
While not rendering the game unplayable or the fights impossible, they make it grueling and unrewarding
The controls are garbage and the combat system is trash
The save system is aggressively punishing and I hit two game-breaking bugs in the first two quests
Finally getting around to playing it and I really like it. It's not QUITE Skyrim, but it is very very good. I will definitely update this as I play.

Yes, this game has its issues. And I care to say that there aren't any "Mount and Blade" style 200v200 battles in this game which I somewhat expected.

Otherwise, it fits very well into the brutal survival/open world genre people have been eating up lately. If you liked Skyrim but disliked how the difficulty of the game varied from dull to horrendous if you had the settings up to Master/Legend, this is the game for you. Decent and unique combat, learning curve, good story, and plenty o' shit to do.

That being said the first time I tried to play this game I started on hardcore mode, which kept me from learning valuable things about the HUD and whatnot, so at least give regular mode a try first.

To hell with all these reviews and complaints. It almost convinced me not to buy this game. I've been starved for a good RPG with side quests and a new take on combat. And this game satisfied my craving like hell.

I have everything on high, fps are on constant 60 and I'm 33 hours in and reached the point on the quest line where you try to find the copper sheets maker. I've had not a single bug, not a single crash, this game ran perfectly for me.

I don't know what I'm doing, how it works but for me this game is worth it and I'm going to play the living crap out of it. Thank you Warhorse Studios for bringing something new to the market and I hope you make more.

I am done with the first part of the game and the world is finally open to me in a sense. The game went way over what my expectations were and I am really enjoying it. I get the same feeling playing this game as I did the first time I played Witcher 3 or Oblivion. The game is really good and I am glad I backed the game during the kickstarter phase.
Most of the people giving the game bad reivews seem to have expected an arcade skyrimish game set in Bohemia and most complaints are from people who seem to have no basic knowledge what so ever on classical RPG mechanics. This game is not Skyirm and they never said they would create a game that was gonna look and act like Skyrim, they wanted a realistic immersive game about the life in 1403 Bohemia which they as far as I know succeeded in doing.

This game in the sale should be a must buy, combat system and immersion are excellent. Also it has some of the most memorable quests ever put to a game, minimal hand holding is also a good thing for this title. The archery learning curve was very satisfying when practice made perfect. 9/10

I'm reviewing this game after completing KCD2 recently. I definitely recommend this game to any RPG fans. 9/10 (-1 point because the sword-fighting game mechanic is much more polished in KCD2. sword-fighting in KCD1 gave me a high bp)

I bought this game 3 days ago and I'm already at 24 hours played. It's crazy how much better the game gets as you get better at it, too... right now I'm stuck in a loop of training, playing dice, and competing in the Rattay tournament. This is the kind of immersion I wish I'd seen in games like Skyrim.

At first the combat felt frustrating, but once you learn perfect-block and master-strike (counterattack), the game becomes a whole different experience. 

That said... dealing with multiple enemies still makes me want to pull my hair out. I'd always rather run away than deal with one guy practically trying to kiss me (one guy try to stay too close to you like trying to push or something) while two other annoying bastards flank me from behind, I can't bro.

The horrifying morality and difficulty of the Witcher games meets the absolute freedom and immersion of the Elder Scrolls games. The high resolution mud textures you'll be staring at just before you die another meaningless death are just as beautiful as the pauses you'll take walking in the forest to stare at another breathtaking sunset peeking through the greenery.

You also can't read any of the books that you find because you're illiterate and combat is as medieval as cutting a steak with a plastic knife, so if you liked reading whatever was lying around Skyrim and pirouetting your socks off with Geralt, this game is not that. You'll learn to read and fight after 20 hours if you're lucky. It's nothing but a morbidly fun and atmospheric misery simulator until then.

Incredibly detailed, realistic and fun RPG. Set in the middle ages you start out as a nobody that doesnt know how to do anything, and you slowly build up your skills. You can choose how you want to play, if you want to be a good or bad guy. A thief, hunter, warrior, alchemist etc theres endless possibilities. The story and quests are great, even the sidequests are fun, sound and music is lovely, and the graphics are gorgeous.

The game world is so lovely and very immersive. If you're interested in history theres a lot to learn in this game too, and its interesting seeing how people lived in the middle ages. Its obvious the developers did a ton of research to make it as realistic as possible.

There are a lot of mods available at nexusmods, if you want to be able to save as often as you like you can use a mod for that. The performance and optimization is pretty good, runs great on my system with R5 2600 and Vega 56.

If you want a realistic RPG to sink your life into, this is the game. I have 45 hrs playtime and am about 3/5 through the main story line. Be aware that some might find it a bit slow, theres not action constantly, you need to be patient.

I really wanted to like this game, but it feels like it doesn't want to be a game. I don't mind the grounded setting, I don't need magic or dragons to have fun.
I think there's a fine line between what can be considered immersion and what can just become an annoyance, even small things like NPCs not wanting to talk to you at night seem fine at first, but then you go to sleep, gotta find a bed, oh that bed is owned, find another one, sleep, oh now you're hungry, deal with that, and before you know it you've had to do a bunch of pre-requisite steps just to hand in a quest. Immersive gameplay shouldn't feel like a chore.

The combat is already a known quantity in terms of being rated poorly, and it really does feel horrible on mouse+KB, I actually started to feel like I was making progress, then I'd rock up to a random bandit camp or whatever and get completely wrecked. The scaling feels a bit all over the place in that regard. "oh you're a peasant you're not meant to be good with a sword" okay, that's great, but immersion becoming a chore rears its ugly head again.

Games provide escapism, and sometimes you just want to feel like the hero, if you're used to more traditional western RPGs in that regard, this game probably isn't for you.
Amazing game. You have to do the work at first to get in the battle rhythm. Go to YouTube and get some advice.

Probably the best medieval game I've ever played, it's not your average hack and slash type of game. You're not a hero, just an ordinary peasant who got his life turned upside down. This game provides a lot of history, which I'm a big fan of.
The best thing about the game is that it's very hardcore, one wrong move and your opponents will kill you. Combat system is very difficult to master, but it's part of the fun.

Since KCD2 is out, it makes this game even more worth to purchase and try it out. Since it takes place immediately after the first game.
10/10, have played this 5 times and can still find something new in the map.

I wanted to like this title and honestly there is a lot to like here, from the story and overall premise of the game. But some of the game mechanics and mainly combat is just way too janky, I will be trying the second title and I urge you to give this one a try as well, as the gameplay might not be a break point for you as it was for me.

One of the best RPGs out there - but you have to give it time.

At first, Kingdom Come: Deliverance will humble you. You’ll lose everything, fail dialogue checks, accidentally try to pickpocket a trader you're staring at, and get beaten senseless by six peasants in the dead of night because you forgot to equip your sword and can’t run fast enough.

That struggle is the point. There are ways to prevent almost all of this (losing everything aside), but the game demands patience and learning. Over time, you grow stronger, smarter, and more capable - until you slowly bend Bohemia to your will.

Stick with it, and you’ll uncover an absolute goldmine of fun. KCD rewards persistence like few RPGs ever have.

This Game is absolutely great - The Stories I experienced so far (only doing Side Quests, not even started the main quests) The characters are so well written. And also it sounds and looks great. Running on Ultra Details around 90fps its a pleasure to play. Can recommend

The first time I played this game it never clicked for me. I got motion sick easily from the head bob, hated not being able to save whenever, and ultimately encountered a bug that left me stuck on my horse with my last save being 2hrs back. For the next several years I ignored this game until I decided to give it another go. I'm pleased to say that playing in windowed mode prevents me from getting motion sick, I use mods liberally to elevate my experience, and so far I've enjoyed the heck out of this game. The beginning is quite a slog but once you get past it, and are free to roam and truly play the game, it's quite fun. If you're like me and don't have the convenience of playing for long periods, absolutely get the mod that allows manual saving whenever. It's necessary for people who have lives.

So far as realistic RPGs come, this is probably the best one so far. The combat system is quite nice, the graphics superb and I love the complexity.

Definitely recommended.

This game always sits im my library unplayed for years, because every time I play i am reminded why I fuckin hate this game. Combat is clunky, and dam near useless. Sword-fighting lessons? useless in an actual fucking fight. Blocking? No thanks, because the shit has the response time of a drunk sloth. Side-step? lol good luck with that bozo. The story is interesting but getting past game-play is fucking terrible.

Since I can't give a neutral review, I will just keep with the negative one.

Don't get me wrong, I must say the game is incredible, and you can see that a lot in other people's reviews. Although, I ended up with a negative review because of the huge ammount of glitches that will appear. Glitches which will make you get stuck in places, glitches which will crash your game, make you die, and it keeps going.

The thing is, this game won't let you save whenever you want, which is for the immersion (I know there are mods that let you save whenever you want, but I will just stick with the vanilla experience). The game only saves on missions, when you close it, and you can also use a potion that saves the game for you, but sometimes that potion may not be available. So, if the game glitches, which will happen a lot, you are able to lose hours of progress if you are not careful enough, and this is why it ended up with a negative review.

So, I should say, play it at your own risk, or, just download a mod that disables that saving system and be happy.

One of the best games I have ever played. But at the same time I can easily see why some people would dislike it. This is not all around masterpiece and I feel it was made to be like that.

This game targets people who like Hardcore RPG games. There are some casual mechanics like fast travel, but mostly it tries to reach for realism.

Everything takes some time to learn and I really like that, it makes me feel very immersed.

There's been some talk about bugs, but I honesly havent come across any that would make me feel like "well that has to be fixed asap"

Game is somewhat poorly optimised, and CPU heavy so keep that in mind.

I really love this game but It's hard to recommend it, because I know that it's definetly not a game for everyone. Trying it out is also pretty much impossible, because Steam only allows refunds for games you have played under 2 hours, and it takes about 5-10 for one to really see if they like the game or not.

This game gives you an amazing outlook over the story and how it follows and ties henry to it, this game is absolutely amazing if someone prefers depth of a story over spectacle. We get to see the rise of Henry and all the political matters that the nobles used to go through with, it is intensely immersive as time will fly by the more you love it. I would recommend this to everyone who loves a story with an amazing depiction of our history and how everything came to be.

Lastly i would say that warhorse studios and everyone they worked with to create this masterpiece, they deserve every bit of love they get and i hope they continue on with their amazing work.
Game mechanics, ambience, graphics, story, side quests true RPG experience thank you Warhorse for this masterpiece

I thoroughly enjoyed this game. The story is well done and the atmosphere is immersive. There are some bugs in there but it's nothing to put you off the game. The combat has a bit of a learning curve but once you invest some time with it, it's very fun and rewarding.

Personal Game Score: 9 / 10

+ Good game graphics
+ Great storyline or plot
+ Immersive Game
+ Great Music
+ Very Enjoyable

- Some bugs and performance glitches

This game is a full imersive medieval experience, with ALL the pros and cons on it...
You are not special and, like life itself, you need to learn and train the skills that you want to master.
Its a realy, realy good and underestimate game, altought its very SLOW paced in comparison with some other rpg-adventure games out there, dont expect to dominate in combat in a short time (you gonna get beated a lot) and will get lost in the map or quests sometimes...
But on a sale, and with some free time, its very much worth it! And go for hardcore mode if you like a lot the medieval experience of horseriding!

I remember playing the Kingdom Come: Deliverance demo a few years ago, it was really sturdy and it barely worked. When the full version released I was very sceptical about the game, especially given that reviews were talking about many technical problems. After all KC:D turned out to be a masterpiece.

I have played this game 3 times, every playthrough was giving me more fun and joy. Kingdome Come: Deliverence is a very well-writen RPG with rich characters and dialogue. You won't experience dull, storyless missions in it. The best parts about the game are the graphics and level design. They are gorgeous!

If you have not tried this game before - now is the time!

This is a hard game to properly review. I bought it a while back but got a refund due to how slow the intro is. An hour into the game and I hand't experience combat aside from an optional training that only teaches you some of the basics. But KCD came on sale again and I decided to give it a second chance and stick with it. And oh boy am I enjoying myself! The map isn't huge, but there is actually a good number of things to do and a lot to explore. I personally find the combat to be fun as long as you aren't fighting more than one person at a time. The biggest bit of advice I can give is get the mod that allows free saves. I don't know why anyone thought it was a good idea to have a consumable as the save system, but it is annoying because you find yourself not saving as to not waste all of your save, then you get ambushed by 5 bandits and they just gangbang you. Or your game crashes, one of the two will happen. Overall, it's hard to get through the begining, but it is worth it in my opinion.

I really enjoyed this game. It really nailed a that classic rpg feeling I hadn't experienced in a while. The only time I felt dissapointed was when it ended. At least I have the second one to look forward to. 10/10 consider my pizzle yanked.

Let me begin by stating how excited I was for this title. It had great reviews, Youtube coverage, critical acclaim, etc. As soon as I could, I grabbed it on sale and started playing.

The beginning is slow. Once you understand the mechanics, how to "level up", get a strong start, etc. the game becomes a glorious intrigue of characters and events you can relate to. ***Keep in mind you MUST make the most of the starting chapter to set yourself up for an enjoyable experience down the line!***

Environment/player interaction is unusual but refreshing. A few bugs still persist to this day but don't negatively impact the game too heavily. Combat, hunger, relationships with NPCs, and even things like bathing are implemented to give you a rich experience.

How could a game so beautiful and compelling let you down?
2 major things:

The absolute TRASH save system. (seriously, what RPG completely discourages saves and makes it a pain the keister to do so???)
AND
The pigeon holed character progression

Edit: 28JUN2020
I tried it again and I am still not convinced. It hurts my soul to see such a gem wasted with crap save system. However, this is a brand new studio tackling a beast of a game. These guys absolutely deserve credit for their hard work. Pick up on sale and immerse yourself in this epic tale based on real events.
The game is good. Yeah, it’s good. Great. Nice. Beautiful. Perfect game and I bought it just to leave a review.

A cry of anger. I've spent here 100 hrs now, and I was ready to wait for new patches to solve the bugs. I've waited for the fix of the 1st critical bug that didn't make it possible to continue the main quest in Pribyslavitz, when all your forces just got stuck and didn't move. I gave this game another chance when I was stuck foir the 2nd time at the main quest line in Vranik and the quest NPC didn't show up. I went for a vacation, returned to the game, reloaded my save and started doing the preparations (again) to visit Vranik (again). I made them all (again) and run for the quest to save myself in front of the gates just ot be sure (again), but a bandit in the forest threw me down from my horse, and for the <who knows the count> time i was stuck in the earth texture (again). Thank you Warhorse.

i would recommend this game however, as good as the story is, and how captivating the scenery is, its one of the hardest games i have ever played (keep in mind ive never played dark souls or elden ring or anything of the sort) im just a casual gamer and for someone who typically plays games on the easiest difficulty, this game is really really hard, ive even had to resort to mods to get rid of the god awful lock picking mini game. and have been spending pretty much my entire play through avoiding battles, and that does make it a lot less fun, and it lacks any proper difficulty options, what you get is what you get, thats it, no options.

This has to be one of the best games I have ever played. The historical accuracy seems pretty on point and the combat is pretty intense especially in the begining, the story is great as well. This is pretty much every thing i have been looking for in a medieval RPG.

I have played through large parts of the game and completed most side quests and completed several of the dlc's. Now when i'm working through the last main missions though i get stuck loading in the quest "Cold Steel, Hot Blood" which is the 25 main quest. It is bugged and after a series of cutscenes it's stuck trying to load. This seems to be a problem going back to 2018 and the devs seems to outright refuse to fix the issue which breaks the main quest progression.

I can't promote a game where the devs have not fixed a critical bug after five years and seems all but abandoned people who reported it and sent in their save files. The only way to progress through this bug seems to download a cheat mod and use it to get past the issue.

Great Game for the genre it attempts to create. Definitely slower pace and the design (combat, horse, animations) can be janky at times but if you like serious RPG simulators, this is the one for you.

Also this is a longer game, I thought it had ended at least twice until it carried on. You will get your monies worth if you but it now on discount.

Try it on hardcore to complete the game and join less than 1% of players to do so.

- be me
- decides to be daring and play on hardcore mode
- dies before the game even begins

10/10 for historical accuracy

My only gripe is the optimization, I believe it could be way better. The combat system can also be frustrating when fighting multiple enemies at the same time. I hope the sequel improves on these.

But it took me 86 hours to finish the game once with all the DLCs in it (which is a very good thing) and this easily quenched my thirst for a proper open world RPG. The industry really needs more games like these.

I nearly gave up on it halfway through.
That combat really is donkey balls. Nearly everything else about the game is great.
It's amusing watching your character go from being beaten up by the local bully and go crying to your mother to a fully fledged knight.
Albeit a knight in patchwork and mix and match armour
Also some of the quests are timed or fail if you do a story mission and the game won't tell you which they are until its too late besides that it's really good.
Amazing game, up there with some of the greatest, if only slightly rough around the edges. Can't wait to get to the sequel!

Pros:
- Cool grounded setting based on real history.
- None of the usual cliche fantasy rpg tropes. Great story and quest design.
- RPG elements. Start off as a unskilled peasant and progress from there.
- Improve at things by doing them. Not the typical experience and leveling mechanics.
- Fun combat system overall.
- Runs really well on older hardware.

Cons:
- In combat there are some ways to perform unblockable attacks which enemies can do to you as well. This makes it quite difficult to land the combos, especially the 4 hit combos, without being interrupted.
- The combat "lock on" to target game mechanic can really work against you when fighting groups of enemies. It is more suited to 1v1 fights.

My experience has left me with a love/hate relationship with this game. On the one hand I do adore the setting and efforts made to create a well-fleshed out, realistic medieval world with an interesting historical story. Many of the systems in the game are well suited to such a styled RPG, like Fallout with the survival mode switch stuck on and broken off, however what lets this game down is the truly terrible combat system, fiddling with odd angles which the AI decides to block and parry no matter what, and other general NPC balance. One can spend over 20 hours grinding combat experience against the NPC trainers and still be felled by the most modest, starving peasant; even after hitting them in the head with a two-handed weapon, while they were sleeping... I simply cannot recommend it to anyone but patient masochists, FEMA experts in awkward mouse combat and the modding community, which may eventually get around to fixing the curve of this rough diamond, that turned out to be a zirconia.

It is love and hate relationship. I'm czech so I love this game because it is czech, made by mr. Vávra and I love those little details in game like some bad words. However I ragequited so many times, mostly because I'm lame in fight and saving drives me crazy. Anyway I recommend this, it's intense, it has the atmosphere and it is challenging.

KCD Is an open world RPG Skyrim type game, and I would recommend it to anyone who is willing to put time and effort into learning a much harder combat system, and doesn't mind slow times in certain areas of the game, especially travelling. After spending much time on the game myself, it has grown to become one of my favorite games on steam, and it is definitely worth a try.
One of the best games i have ever played, yes at first you suck, but be patient and crack on, it will get better. With training and development of the character.

A more realistic approach to a medieval life. Start off as a peasant who can't fight at all to someone who does pretty well in combat. Combat is challenging and even at end game it was tough without strategy. It took awhile for me to get into this game. My suggestion is to follow the main quest line until you can read / get a horse then proceed how you see fit. If you're struggling with combat enroll in the tournaments, enter archery contests, and train outside of Rattay to up your combat skills. Once this game hooked me I relaxed and enjoyed the ride. If you want constant action, this isnt the game for you. You enhance the gameplay with a bit of role play and handling situations as you see fit (stealth, combat, maybe a speech check).

Some quests are timed yet aren't mentioned as timed so listen or read the dialog to get the hint.

I don't remember ever playing a game with so many bugs, but at the same time, it was so fun to play :D
Can be frustrating at the start, but hold on, it'll pay off :)

I got this game on Christmas and beat it today, it is amazing, the story is great, the graphics are great, the bugs are slight, and the game play is awesome! I wish I had done more before the end, and I hope through DLC or a sequel I'll be able to get what I want(going to check dlc now)

The game is annoying. I've never played a game that is so annoying to control, trying to do anything is annoying. After 7 hours, I've barely made progress into the story. Monster Hunter Combat is more fluid than whatever this is. 

If you only want to play casually, I don't recommend buying this game. This game feels like its made for people who have too much time or likes to suffer.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance - A Medieval Gem You Need to Play! 

Kingdom Come: Deliverance is a game that’s as much a love letter to medieval history as it is an engaging RPG. With stunning graphics and a richly detailed environment, it transports you straight into 15th-century Bohemia.You can almost feel the breeze rustling through the trees or smell the smoke from village fires. It’s not just about eye candy, though—the attention to detail creates an immersive world that feels alive.

Sure, the game has a few quirks and bugs here and there. But, as the developers humorously put it, "These are features!" Even if your horse occasionally forgets how to be a horse, it’s hard to stay mad when the rest of the game is this captivating.

The storyline is where Kingdom Come: Deliverance truly shines. It’s complex, authentic, and incredibly well-written. Take, for example, the "Madonna of Sasau" quest—a DLC side story that’s not just a throwaway mission but one of the most gripping narratives you’ll find in any game. Every dialogue feels natural, and you will never want to rip your hair out at the silliness described there. 

The anticipation for Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is real, and if it builds on what the first game delivered, we’re in for another adventure full of history, drama, and plenty of "features."
